question_text: [Cloud Compute, Containers & Serverless - Q57] Why must a Network Access Control List (NACL) rule explicitly permit ephemeral return ports (e.g. 1024-65535) for outbound client connections, while a Security Group does not?

options.text: Security Groups are stateful (automatically permitting return response traffic regardless of inbound rules), while NACLs are stateless (evaluating outbound response traffic independently against outbound rules)
NACLs only operate on UDP traffic
Security Groups execute inside the operating system kernel
NACLs do not support IP CIDR blocks

answer_explanation: Security groups track connection state: if inbound traffic is allowed, corresponding response traffic is automatically allowed outbound. Stateless NACLs evaluate outbound traffic afresh against explicit outbound rules.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: A. Rationale: Security groups track connection state: if inbound traffic is allowed, corresponding response traffic is automatically allowed outbound. Stateless NACLs evaluate outbound traffic afresh against explicit outbound rules.
